To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methanol is a significant intermediate in the anaerobic oxidation of organic matter in subseaflower sediments.
methanol is a significant carbon source for the deep biosphere and that methanol turnover is mediated by methanogenesis, CO2 fixation, and oxidation.
methanol is rapidly consumed in marine sediments, and this consumption is balanced by microbial methanol production, resulting in the maintenance of a constant methanol level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biogeochemical cycle of methanol in the anoxic deep sea sediments.
the biogeochemical cycle of methanol in marine subsurface sediments, which has been largely unknown until now.
the biological flux and lifetime (half-life) of methanol in marine sediments and the biogeochemical cycling of methanol in the oceanic subsurface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
methanol is a key intermediate for the microbial carbon cycle in subseaflower sediments.

the methanol cycle in anoxic sediments is a dynamic process with a significant flux of methanol from microbial sources to sinks, which may be important in controlling the methanol inventory in the deep ocean.
methanol is an important intermediate in anaerobic carbon cycling in marine sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methanol flux in subseaflower sediments is a net sink.

the methanol flux from the overlying seawater to the subseafloor is balanced by methanol production and oxidation in the sediment, and that methanol is not an important source for methane in the sediment.
the methanol cycle in the subseafloor sediment is a closed cycle with a net production rate of 2.5 μmol cm−2 yr−1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methanol is a significant intermediate of anaerobic microbial metabolism in subseafloors sediments.
methanol plays a central role in the anaerobic oxidation of organic carbon in subseafloors sediments.
methanol is an important carbon source for anaerobic microorganisms in the subseafloor biosphere.
